newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC raises wheat and barley stocks, cuts maize.
newsitem.headline: ONIC raises wheat and barley stocks, cuts maize.

text.p: France's ONIC grain office confirmed on Wednesday it had raised its forecasts for 1996/97 soft wheat and barley carryover stocks and had trimmed the forecast for maize.
In a monthly supply/demand report, it projected soft wheat carryover stocks on June 30 of 2.268 million tonnes compared with a previous estimate of 2.120 million tonnes.
It pegged the barley carryover at 873,000 tonnes, against 829,000 tonnes forecast last month, and maize at 2.3 million tonnes compared with a previous estimate of 2.364 million.
The changes were in line with expectations.
ONIC cut its estimate for 1996/97 soft wheat exports to non-EU countries to 6.3 million tonnes from 6.45 million forecast last month and 3.75 million exported in 1995/96.
But this was partly offset by a rise in exports to other EU states to a new record of 9.42 million tonnes, up from 9.36 million last month and 8.613 million last season.
The crop season runs from July to June.
The higher forecast for barley stocks was led by a rise in supplies available to the market after on-farm consumption, to 7.68 million tonnes from 7.62 million projected last month.
ONIC also confirmed it was raising its estimate for barley exports to non-EU countries to 1.6 million tonnes from 1.5 million forecast last month and just 221,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
ONIC shaved carryover stocks for maize to 2.3 million tonnes from last month's forecast of 2.364 million tonnes. This would compare with stocks of 1.647 million tonnes on June 30, 1996.
